tools.name: list_sites
tools.title: List the sites
tools.description: List the sites the current user can view, each with its site_id, type, name, label, description and whether it is displayed in the sites menu. Without a keyword: the portal sites. With a keyword: the portal sites whose name or label contains it, and the group sites whose own name contains it; a space's site is named after the group the space was created with (/spaces/<name at creation>), which a later rename of the space does not change, so a renamed space is found by its original name, not by its label (at most 50 group sites are looked up). Use the site_id in get_site and list_site_pages.

keyword.description: A text the portal site's name or label, or the group site's name (for a space, the name it was created with), must contain; it is what lists a space's site. Omit for the portal sites alone

tools.name: get_site
tools.title: Get a site and its layout
tools.description: Read a site's properties (label, description, banner, access and edit permissions) and its layout: left_sidebar, right_sidebar, topbars and bottom_bars, each with its container_id, options (height or width, sticky, display), styling and the applications it holds with their application_id. Returns the user's site draft when they have one (draft: true), the published layout otherwise.

tools.name: list_site_pages
tools.title: List the pages of a site
tools.description: List the navigation items of a site as a tree. Each item carries its node_id, name and labels per language, url_name, type (page, link or group), page_ref, a link's url, the target the menus open an item's page with (same_tab or new_tab, as the item's tab switch stores it; none on a group), icon, visibility and schedule, the page's access_permissions and edit_permission, and its children. Draft items are never listed; hidden items are listed only when include_hidden is true and the user can edit the site's navigation. Use the page_ref in get_page_layout.

include_hidden.description: Also list the hidden items; omit to list the visible ones only

tools.name: get_page_layout
tools.title: Get the layout of a page
tools.description: Read the whole page in the shape set_page_layout takes: its ordered sections, each with its section_id and type (dynamic: columns and columns_content, one ordered list of applications per column; grid: rows, columns and cells with their cell_id, row, column, spans and application), the styling and display of sections and applications, and every application's application_id, content_id, instance_id and title. Returns the user's draft by default when they have one, the published layout otherwise; version selects one explicitly.

page_ref.description: The page reference, from list_site_pages (for example portal::mysite::home)

version.description: draft reads the user's draft and fails when they have none; published reads the live layout; omit to read the draft when it exists, the published layout otherwise

tools.name: list_layout_applications
tools.title: List the applications that can be placed
tools.description: List the applications the current user can place on a page or in a site container, each with its instance_id, content_id, name, description, category and whether it is configurable through configure_layout_applications. category_id narrows the list to one category, keyword to the names and descriptions containing it.

category_id.description: A category identifier; omit for every category

keyword.description: A text the name or description must contain; omit for no filter

tools.name: create_site
tools.title: Create a site
tools.description: Create a portal site from a site template, as the sites administration does, for every user at once (not a draft). name is the site's identifier and URL segment (letters, digits, - and _; at most 200 characters) and can never change; label is the name users see, in the platform's default language. Options omitted take the administration's defaults: the basic template, not displayed in the sites menu, the fa-globe icon, and administrators as the only ones who can access and edit the site. Every value is checked before anything is written, and a refused one is answered naming the option. The banner takes a banner_upload_id obtained from upload_layout_image. Returns the site as stored after the creation, its site_id included, whatever the permissions written let the caller read afterwards.

name.description: The site identifier: letters, digits, - and _ only, unique among the portal sites, immutable

label.description: The name shown to users, at most 200 characters

description.description: The site description, at most 2000 characters; omit for none

template.description: The layout name of the site template to create the site from, one of the enabled site templates: basic (default), public, spacePublic, or a template an administrator added

banner_upload_id.description: The upload_id of the banner image, from upload_layout_image; omit for no banner

access_permissions.description: Who can access the site, one or more permissions; omit for administrators only. A permission as the sites administration writes it: Everyone, or <membership>:<group> with an existing membership type (* for any) and an existing group, for example *:/platform/users, *:/platform/administrators, member:/spaces/marketing

edit_permission.description: Who can edit the site, one permission; omit for administrators only. A permission as the sites administration writes it, <membership>:<group> with an existing membership type (* for any) and an existing group, for example *:/platform/users, *:/platform/administrators, member:/spaces/marketing

displayed.description: Show the site in the sites menu; omit for not displayed

icon.description: The icon shown in the sites menu, a Font Awesome class name such as fa-globe; omit for fa-globe

tools.name: update_site
tools.title: Update a site
tools.description: Update a site's label, description, icon, display in the sites menu, banner and permissions, as the sites administration does, for every user at once (not a draft). Only a site the sites administration lists can be updated: a portal site that is not a space's public site; a space's site, a user's site or a template is refused. Every option omitted keeps its stored value; a site's name identifies it and cannot change: change the label instead. label and description are written in the platform's default language; translations in other languages are kept. Permissions are written first, then the properties; when the properties fail, the stored permissions are put back. The banner takes a banner_upload_id from upload_layout_image, or remove_banner true to drop the stored one (not both). A refused value is answered naming the option and nothing is changed; when a later step fails, what was written before it is put back. Returns the site as stored after the change, whatever the permissions written let the caller read afterwards.

label.description: The name shown to users, at most 200 characters; omit to keep it

description.description: The site description, at most 2000 characters, an empty string to clear it; omit to keep it

access_permissions.description: Who can access the site, one or more permissions replacing the stored ones; omit to keep them. A permission as the sites administration writes it: Everyone, or <membership>:<group> with an existing membership type (* for any) and an existing group, for example *:/platform/users, *:/platform/administrators, member:/spaces/marketing

edit_permission.description: Who can edit the site, one permission; omit to keep it. A permission as the sites administration writes it, <membership>:<group> with an existing membership type (* for any) and an existing group, for example *:/platform/users, *:/platform/administrators, member:/spaces/marketing

displayed.description: Show the site in the sites menu; omit to keep it; false is refused on the platform's main site, which is always shown

icon.description: The icon shown in the sites menu, a Font Awesome class name such as fa-globe; omit to keep it

banner_upload_id.description: The upload_id of the new banner image, from upload_layout_image; omit to keep the banner

remove_banner.description: true removes the stored banner; omit to keep it

tools.name: delete_site
tools.title: Delete a site
tools.description: Delete a site with its pages and navigation, for every user at once and without undo, as the sites administration does: in the platform's assistant the user confirms it before it applies; an external client asks for confirmation only if its own settings do. A site the administration never offers to delete is refused: one the platform ships as not removable, a space's site or public site, a user's site, a template.

tools.name: update_theme
tools.title: Update a part of the theme
tools.description: Update one part of the platform theme, as the corresponding drawer of the Branding and Theme administration does, for every user at once (not a draft): in the platform's assistant the user confirms it before it applies; an external client asks for confirmation only if its own settings do. options sets the named options to the given values (strings, as the drawer sends them: colours as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA, sizes with their unit such as 16px, keywords such as normal or bold); reset returns the named options to their configured default; every other option keeps its stored value. Options per part. colors: primaryColor, secondaryColor, tertiaryColor. font: fontFamily, one of the platform's supported families. topbar: topBarBackgroundColor, topBarBackgroundPosition, topBarBackgroundSize, topBarBackgroundRepeat, topBarTextColor, topBarTextFontSize, topBarTextFontStyle, topBarTextFontWeight, topBarIconColor, topBarSticky (true or false), topBarBackgroundScrollColor (the colour once scrolled, when sticky). sidebars: sideBarBackgroundColor, sideBarBackgroundImage, sideBarBackgroundPosition, sideBarBackgroundSize, sideBarBackgroundRepeat, sideBarTextColor, sideBarTextFontSize, sideBarTextFontStyle, sideBarTextFontWeight, sideBarTextSubtitleColor, sideBarTextSubtitleFontSize, sideBarTextSubtitleFontStyle, sideBarTextSubtitleFontWeight, sideBarIconColor. drawers: drawerBackgroundColor, drawerBackgroundImage, drawerBackgroundPosition, drawerBackgroundSize, drawerBackgroundRepeat, drawerIconColor, then Color, FontSize, FontStyle and FontWeight for each of drawerText, drawerTextSubtitle, drawerTextTitle and drawerTextHeader (for example drawerTextTitleColor). Every option ending in BackgroundImage takes none or exactly one CSS gradient function, such as linear-gradient(90deg, #ffffff, #000000): the image file itself is uploaded in the drawer, and a url() or a second layer is refused. page_and_apps: pageWidth (100px to 3000px, or 100%), pageBackgroundColor (a hex colour), pageBackgroundEffect (one CSS gradient function, or none), pageBackgroundSize, pageBackgroundRepeat, pageBackgroundPosition, pageBackgroundAttachment (CSS keywords), pageMarginTop, pageMarginRight, pageMarginBottom, pageMarginLeft, appMarginTop, appMarginRight, appMarginBottom, appMarginLeft, appBorderColor, appBorderSize, appBoxShadow, borderRadius, appBorderRadiusTopLeft, appBorderRadiusTopRight, appBorderRadiusBottomLeft, appBorderRadiusBottomRight, appBackgroundColor, appBackgroundImage, appBackgroundPosition, appBackgroundSize, appBackgroundRepeat, appIconColor, then Color, FontSize, FontStyle and FontWeight for each of appText, appTextTitle, appTextHeader and appTextSubtitle, and Color, Image, Position, Size, Repeat, PaddingTop, PaddingRight, PaddingBottom, PaddingLeft and Radius for each of appTextTitleBackground and appTextHeaderBackground. Images (logo, favicon, background files) are not theme options. A value the platform refuses is answered with its reason and nothing is changed. Returns the part's options as stored.

part.description: The part of the theme to update

options.description: The options of the part to set, by name, with their values as strings; omit an option to leave it unchanged

reset.description: The options of the part to return to their configured default; omit for none; an option cannot be both set and reset

tools.name: update_navigation_display
tools.title: Update what the topbar and the sidebar show
tools.description: Update what the topbar shows and how the sidebar may be displayed, as the navigation settings page does, for every user at once (not a draft): in the platform's assistant the user confirms it before it applies; an external client asks for confirmation only if its own settings do. Every field omitted keeps its stored value. topbar: display_company_name, display_site_name, display_mobile_company_logo, and applications, a list of {id or name, enabled, mobile} merged into the topbar's applications: an entry names its application by id (as this tool returns it) or, without an id, by its name as shown in the topbar settings in the user's language (case-insensitive, refused when two applications share it); an application not in the topbar is refused; mobile also shows the application on mobile; the order of the applications is not changed by this tool. sidebar: allow_user_custom_home, allowed_modes (replaces the list; hidden, icon or sticky, at least one), default_mode (one of the allowed modes). The sidebar's items are not changed by this tool. Returns both parts as stored, each topbar application with its id and its name in the user's language.

topbar.description: What the topbar shows; omit to leave the topbar unchanged

display_company_name.description: Show the company name next to the logo as the platform's identity: on wide screens when the sidebar is hidden or reduced to icons, or when no site name or logo is shown; on medium screens only when no site name or logo is shown

display_mobile_company_logo.description: Show the company logo on mobile

applications.description: The topbar applications to change, each named by id or by name; omit to leave them all

id.description: The application identifier, as returned by this tool; omit to name the application by its name

name.description: The application name as shown in the topbar settings in the user's language, used when no id is given

enabled.description: Show the application in the topbar

sidebar.description: How the sidebar may be displayed; omit to leave the sidebar unchanged

allow_user_custom_home.description: Let each user choose their own home page

allowed_modes.description: The modes users may choose from, replacing the stored list; at least one

default_mode.description: The mode a user gets before choosing one; must be an allowed mode

tools.name: set_site_layout
tools.title: Set the layout of a site
tools.description: Replace the structure of the site layout shared by every page of the site, in the current user's draft, as the site layout editor does: the left and right sidebars, the topbars and the bottom bars, each with its options, styling and applications. What is sent is the whole structure, as get_site returns it: a sidebar omitted is removed, topbars or bottom_bars omitted means none. Ids address the layout get_site returned (the user's draft when they have one, the published layout otherwise): a container_id keeps the stored container (a topbar its cells), an application_id keeps the application with its settings, an application given by instance_id or content_id is added, and an application of the layout absent from the call is removed. Nothing is visible to other users until publish_layout; discard_layout_draft starts again from the published layout. On a kept container or application, an option, a styling block or a display omitted keeps what it holds; enabled false clears a block. A site whose stored layout holds two sidebars on one side, which get_site reports as one, is refused. At most 200 containers and applications in one call. Every value is checked before anything is written; a refused value is answered naming the option. Returns the draft as get_site does, with the ids to use in later calls; after publish_layout the ids change, read the site again. New images are not accepted by this tool: a stored image stays unless its background block is turned off.

container_id.description: the id of a sidebar in the layout get_site returned, to keep its stored element; omit to create it

options.description: the container options; an option omitted keeps the stored value on a kept container

width.description: the width in pixels, 50 to 1000; omit to keep it (310 on a new sidebar)

sticky.description: true to keep the sidebar in place when the page scrolls; omit to keep the stored choice

display.description: omit to keep it (both on a new sidebar)

full_height.description: true when the sidebar spans the topbars and bottom bars, false when it sits between them; omit to keep its place (spanning on a new sidebar)

styling.description: the styling blocks as get_site returns them: a block omitted keeps what the element holds (nothing on a new one), a block with enabled false clears it, and inside a block a value omitted keeps the stored one; a stored image stays unless its block is turned off

margins.description: enabled, then all or top/right/bottom/left, -60 to 60 (0 none)

background.description: enabled, then mode solid (default, color) or linear, radial, angular (from, to, ratio 0 to 100 default 50, direction: linear to_bottom default or to_right, angular top_left default, top_right, bottom_right or bottom_left); colours as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA; scroll_color: the solid colour once scrolled, sticky containers only; a topbar takes a solid colour only; a new image is not accepted here

text.description: enabled, icon_color, then title, header, content and subtitle, each {color, size 1 to 60, bold, italic}; title and header also take background {enabled, mode solid (default, color) or linear, radial, angular (from, to, ratio 0 to 100 default 50, direction: linear to_bottom default or to_right, angular top_left default, top_right, bottom_right or bottom_left); colours as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA, padding {top, right, bottom, left} -400 to 400, corners {enabled, all or each corner 0 to 120}}; a value omitted is kept, a new image is not accepted here

content_id.description: the application content id to add, from list_layout_applications, when exactly one enabled catalog instance has it; omit when application_id or instance_id is given

tools.name: publish_layout
tools.title: Publish the draft of a site layout
tools.description: Make the current user's site draft the published layout, for every user at once, as the site layout editor's publish does: in the platform's assistant the user confirms it before it applies; an external client asks for confirmation only if its own settings do. Fails when the user has no draft of the site. The draft ends and every container and application takes a new id: returns the site as published, with the new ids.

tools.name: discard_layout_draft
tools.title: Discard the draft of a site layout
tools.description: Drop the current user's site draft and start a new one from the published layout, as the site layout editor's "start again" does; nothing published changes. Fails when the user has no draft of the site. Returns the new draft, with its ids.

tools.name: create_page
tools.title: Create a navigation item
tools.description: Create a navigation item of a site with the inputs of the navigation's 'Add an item' drawer, for every user at once (not a draft). visible false keeps the item out of the menus and the lists only: its page stays reachable at its address (the site's, then the url_name of each ancestor item and its own) by whoever its access_permissions admit, so a page under construction is kept from users by access_permissions naming its editors' or reviewers' group, widened when the item is made visible. The item goes last under its parent, the site's root when parent_node_id is omitted. type decides what it points to: page creates a new page from a page template (page_template_id, the catalog's first blank template when omitted); existing_page points at a page given by page_ref; link creates a link page opening url, in the same or a new tab (target); group points at nothing. url_name is the item's segment in the page address, chosen now and never changed afterwards: letters, digits, - and _, unique among its siblings; omit it to derive it from the label as the drawer does. access_permissions and edit_permission are written on the page created here (a page or a link); omitted, the site's apply; they are refused on an existing page, whose permissions update_page changes, and on a group. Every value is checked before anything is written; the page is created first, then the item, and a page left behind by an item failure is removed. Returns the item as list_site_pages describes it, with its node_id and page_ref.

parent_node_id.description: The node_id of the item the new one goes under, from list_site_pages; omit for the site's root

label.description: The name shown to users, in the platform's default language, at most 200 characters

labels.description: The name per language, keyed by a language tag the platform supports (en, fr, ...), for the languages other than the platform's default one, whose text is label; an entry set to null is ignored

url_name.description: The item's segment in the page address: letters, digits, - and _, at most 200 characters, unique among its siblings; chosen at creation and never changed. Omit to derive it from the label as the drawer does (accents and other characters dropped, lower case)

type.description: page: a new page from a page template; existing_page: the page page_ref names; link: a link to url; group: a group of pages, pointing at nothing

page_template_id.description: For a page: the identifier of an enabled page template; omit for the catalog's first blank template. Refused for any other type

page_ref.description: For an existing page: the page reference, from list_site_pages (for example portal::mysite::home), of a page the user can view. Refused for any other type

url.description: For a link: an absolute http or https address with a host, or a site-relative path starting with one /; any other scheme and //host are refused. Refused for any other type

target.description: For an item pointing at a page (a page, an existing page or a link): same_tab (the default) or new_tab, where the menus open it, as list_site_pages reads it back; omit for same_tab. Refused for a group

icon.description: The icon shown in the navigation, a Font Awesome class name such as fa-home or fas fa-home; omit for none

visible.description: Whether users see the item in the menus and the lists; omit for true. It does not restrict the page's address: access_permissions do

scheduled.description: When the item is visible: both start and end as ISO-8601 date-times with an offset or Z (2026-11-01T09:00:00Z), the start after now and the end after the start; refused on an item made hidden; omit for no schedule

access_permissions.description: Who can view the page, one or more permissions as the sites administration writes them: Everyone, or <membership>:<group> with an existing membership type (* for any) and an existing group, for example *:/platform/users, member:/spaces/marketing; omit for the site's. Refused for an existing page and a group

edit_permission.description: Who can edit the page, one permission as the sites administration writes it, <membership>:<group>, for example *:/platform/administrators; omit for the site's. Refused for an existing page and a group

tools.name: update_page
tools.title: Update a navigation item
tools.description: Update a navigation item's name and translations, type, icon, visibility and schedule, and the permissions of its page, as the navigation drawer's edit does, for every user at once (not a draft). Every option omitted keeps its stored value; a translation given is merged over the stored ones; the label replaces the item's bundle-provided name when the item has none stored. The URL name is chosen at creation and cannot change: a url_name different from the stored one is refused with the reason 'cannot be changed: url_name'. A type given follows the drawer's edit: group detaches the page; existing_page points the item at page_ref; link rewrites the link page's url, or creates a link page when the item had none; page creates a new page from page_template_id (the catalog's first blank template when omitted) when the item had no page or a link, and on an item already pointing at a page only when page_template_id is given, so the type read back from list_site_pages can be sent back unchanged; a replaced page is kept, under no item, so repeating such a call leaves a page behind each time. An item whose page no longer exists is still read as a page and keeps its reference: type group drops it, page_ref points it elsewhere, and type page without page_template_id changes nothing on it. Without type, page_ref alone re-points the item, url alone rewrites a link item's address, page_template_id is refused. access_permissions and edit_permission are written on the item's page, merged with its current ones, which needs the right to edit that page; they are refused on a group and in a call that points the item at another page (page_ref): point first, then change that page's permissions in a second call. visible false hides the item and drops its schedule; a scheduled object with neither bound drops the schedule and keeps the item visible. The page steps come first, then the item, and what was written is put back when a later step fails. Returns the item as list_site_pages describes it.

label.description: The name shown to users, in the platform's default language, at most 200 characters; omit to keep it

labels.description: The name per language, keyed by a language tag the platform supports (en, fr, ...), for the languages other than the platform's default one, whose text is label; a language omitted keeps its stored translation, an entry set to null is ignored

url_name.description: Cannot be changed: a value different from the stored one is refused with that reason; omit it

type.description: The new kind of the item; omit to keep it. page: a new page from a page template; existing_page: the page page_ref names; link: a link to url; group: a group of pages

page_template_id.description: With type page: the identifier of an enabled page template; omit for the catalog's first blank template. Refused otherwise

page_ref.description: The page reference, from list_site_pages, of a page the user can view, to point the item at; with type existing_page or alone, and without permissions. Refused with another type

url.description: For a link item: an absolute http or https address with a host, or a site-relative path starting with one /; any other scheme and //host are refused; omit to keep it. Refused on an item that is not a link unless type is link

target.description: For an item pointing at a page (a page, an existing page or a link): same_tab or new_tab, where the menus open it, as list_site_pages reads it back; omit to keep it, through a type change too. Refused for a group

icon.description: The icon shown in the navigation, a Font Awesome class name such as fa-home or fas fa-home; omit to keep it

visible.description: Whether users see the item in the menus and the lists; omit to keep it. false hides the item and drops its schedule; true shows it, keeping a stored schedule. It does not restrict the page's address: access_permissions do

scheduled.description: When the item is visible: both start and end as ISO-8601 date-times with an offset or Z (2026-11-01T09:00:00Z), the start after now and the end after the start; refused on an item made hidden; omit to keep the stored schedule; an object with neither bound drops it

access_permissions.description: Who can view the page, one or more permissions as the sites administration writes them: Everyone, or <membership>:<group> with an existing membership type (* for any) and an existing group, for example *:/platform/users, member:/spaces/marketing; omit to keep them. Refused for a group and together with page_ref

edit_permission.description: Who can edit the page, one permission as the sites administration writes it, <membership>:<group>, for example *:/platform/administrators; omit to keep it. Refused for a group and together with page_ref

tools.name: delete_page
tools.title: Delete a navigation item
tools.description: Delete a navigation item with the items under it, for every user at once and without undo, as the navigation drawer does after its confirmation: in the platform's assistant the user confirms it before it applies; an external client asks for confirmation only if its own settings do. The page the item pointed to is kept, as the drawer keeps it, under no item. An item the platform manages itself is refused.
